rule14_note: Vision model describes OUR OWN test screenshots. Origin/path only; never target page content for identification.

calls.name: run2-failing-case
calls.description:
In the “CSS Demo: justify-content” widget near the bottom, the editable code field showing `justify-content: start;` has changed:

- It now has a blue focus outline around the input.
- A small blue right-pointing arrow/chevron button has appeared on the right edge of that input field.

Everything else on the page — the top banner, navigation, left sidebar, right “In this article” menu, headings, text, and baseline browser icons — looks identical between the two screenshots.

calls.name: run4-reduce-clutter
calls.description: A small right-pointing chevron icon (`>`) has appeared at the right edge of the `justify-content: start;` code box in the “Try it” section; this arrow was not visible in the first screenshot. Everything else on the page appears unchanged.

calls.name: run5-hn-spacing
calls.description:
**Increased vertical spacing and header size.** The orange Hacker News header bar is much taller in the second screenshot, taking up roughly twice the vertical space, and the "Hacker News" logo text appears larger/bolder. 

**Story list is more spread out.** The vertical gap between each numbered story entry is significantly larger, so only stories 1–7 are visible in the second screenshot instead of 1–20 in the first.

**Story metadata appears lighter.** The secondary text showing points, submitter, time, `hide`, and comment counts is rendered in a lighter gray and sits farther below each title.

**Overall density reduced.** The same content exists but the page now shows less of it at once, with substantially more whitespace between elements.

calls.name: red-v4-user-important.png
calls.description:
The page has a bright red background overall. Centre-top is a white rectangular content box containing:

- Heading: “Cascade Origin Test Page”
- Text explaining: “This page has an unlayered body { background: #f6f6ef } rule. User-origin CSS should beat it; author-origin normal should not.”
- A small green boxed element labelled: “Variant 5 target — JS sets `background: green !important` inline.”
- Two result notes: “If the background is red, the CSS beat the unlayered rule.” and “If the #v5-box is green, inline important won. If red, user important won.”

So: page background is red, the outer content box is white, and the inner test box is green.
